chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Abu Ali ibn Rashid, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Your mawali have differed, so can I pray behind them all?' He said, 'Do not pray except behind the one whom you trust in his religion.' Then he said, 'And I have mawali.' I said, 'Companions?' He said, interrupting before I finished mentioning them, 'Did Ali ibn Hadeed instruct you with this, or is this from what you have been instructed by Ali ibn Hadeed?' I said, 'Yes.'
ai.seo_question: Who should one pray behind according to Imam al-Sadiq when followers differ?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the principle of *taqiyya* and selective trust in the early Shia community, where 'mawali' (clients/followers) were not uniformly reliable due to varying degrees of adherence and potential concealment of faith. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between general companions and specific trusted individuals, using Ali ibn Hadeed as a benchmark to illustrate that prayer validity depends on the Imam's personal assurance of the follower's religious integrity rather than mere association. This reflects the historical context of the Abbasid era, where political pressure necessitated a nuanced approach to communal leadership and ritual authority.
